question: Does a pre-instrument semantic contrast from a non-Orientale Artemis II observation agree with independent LOLA roughness values strongly enough to justify a larger controlled multi-target test?
terminal_objective: Test the cheapest credible fragment of the semantic cross-instrument hypothesis without reviving the retired sub-resolution claim or widening to bulk archive analysis.
baseline: The transcript contrast may be fully explained by obvious crater morphology, geologic age, illumination, albedo, coarse localization, or one observer's language; no instrument concordance is assumed.
treatment: Freeze the Vavilov-rougher versus Hertzsprung-smoother semantic direction before reading LOLA values, then compare equal-size disks centered on official USGS coordinates across the 57 m, 225 m, and 560 m LOLA median-absolute-slope products.

regions.rule: Use every valid raster pixel whose center lies within the great-circle radius of the official feature center. Use identical physical radii for both targets.

acquisition.method: HTTP byte-range requests for the smallest complete latitude-row strip covering both 30 km disks in each raster
acquisition.replay: Verification runs only from pinned local strips and receipts.

claim_ceiling: A pass establishes only coarse directional concordance for one same-observer, two-target contrast under fixed map sampling. It does not establish causation, perception below resolution, observer generality, independence from geology or morphology, statistical significance, novelty, or a publishable scientific result.

next_step_logic.if_pass: Admit one larger prospectively coded multi-target test with competing map layers, morphology and geologic-unit controls, illumination and viewing metadata, and at least one additional observer if available.
next_step_logic.if_fail: Stop the semantic roughness lane and retain NASA's qualitative Orientale interpretation only.
next_step_logic.if_indeterminate: Stop acquisition and repair only the named source or localization boundary if existing metadata can do so without bulk imagery.
